source.author: verg
source.text: Iamque dies epulata novem gens omnis, et aris factus honos: placidi straverunt aequora venti, creber et aspirans rursus vocat Auster in altum.
source.text_original: Iamque dies epulata novem gens omnis, et aris / factus honos: placidi straverunt aequora venti, / creber et aspirans rursus vocat Auster in altum.
source.text_english: And now the whole people had feasted for nine days, and honor had been paid to the altars: the gentle winds had smoothed the sea, and the south wind, blowing often and again, called them back to the deep.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at cuncti fremere intus et aequora venti poscere.
reuse.text_original: at cuncti fremere intus et aequora venti / poscere.
reuse.text_english: But all within were roaring and demanding the seas for the winds.
